headline: Shared filesystem write and subprocess capability create medium-risk conflict and prompt-injection pathways; no direct evidence of cross-agent parsing or data leakage.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A can read/write files and build shared context; Agent B has no documented isolation or parsing safeguards. A plausible pathway is A writing instruction-like content into shared files that B later consumes, but the exact bridge is undocumented, so uncertainty pushes this above low. Both profiles show file-oriented surfaces or lack thereof, but no direct evidence of a shared channel.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or file tree, A can place instruction-like content for B to read.
IF B consumes file contents as trusted input, injected instructions can influence downstream behavior.
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct directories.
Add a manual review step before B consumes A-authored files.
Prefix A outputs with machine-readable metadata only.
requires-engineering: enforce provenance tags on all shared files.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches marketing content and product marketing context and can write files; B has no documented data classes touched and no network egress. There is no evidence of a shared workspace or third-party upload path, so leakage is possible only if operators co-locate files. Because the pairwise data path is undocumented, this stays low rather than none.
conditions: IF A and B share a filesystem containing sensitive marketing materials, B could read them.
IF B is configured to ingest files from A's workspace, those contents may be exposed in B outputs.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of any shared directory.
Run B on a separate workspace with read-only inputs.
Review B outputs before external sharing.
requires-engineering: add per-agent access controls on shared storage.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, while B has no explicit write or concurrency controls documented. If both are attached to the same mutable directory, A can overwrite artifacts B depends on, causing conflicts. The absence of locking or coordination in B makes the overlap plausible in default operator setups, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, file clobbering or race conditions can occur.
IF either agent mutates shared state without locks, concurrent runs can diverge.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Serialize runs when both touch the same project.
Use file locks around shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add transactional writes for shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is designed around shared context and marketing content generation, while B is a data-engineering/automation tool with job-scheduler tags. If B treats A's generated text as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream automation or reporting. No verification mechanism is documented for B, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF B ingests A-produced text without validation, A's mistakes can propagate.
IF B triggers scheduled actions from A's outputs, downstream errors can multiply.
mitigations: Require human review of A outputs before B uses them.
Add schema validation to A-to-B handoffs.
Limit B to read-only analysis of A outputs.
requires-engineering: implement confidence thresholds before automation.

E_compliance.rationale: A is an open-source marketing skill with allowlisted egress and documented file surfaces; B has no documented sensitive data classes, residency, or retention obligations. No compliance mismatch is evidenced, but the profiles are sparse and unverified, so only a low-risk gap can be asserted. B is not cited for a specific violation because none is documented.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into A's marketing workflow, compliance obligations may change.
IF B is later configured to store or export personal data, retention and residency review is needed.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in either agent.
Document data-class handling before deployment.
Review retention settings for any shared storage.
requires-engineering: add policy checks for regulated datasets.
